Figure 2. Overview of the DGSIP attack. Our framework employs an unaligned guide model (𝐿𝐿 ), prepared by fine-tuning on harmful
datasets, to guide a coordinated attack against a target VLM (𝐿𝑀 ) by alternating between two modules. First, a dissonance-guided search
iteratively refines a textual su!x by exploiting the predictive dissonance between the two models. When this search stalls, an image-phrase
module is triggered, which uses 𝐿𝐿 to select a potent phrase and Bayesian Optimization to tune its rendering parameters.

the dominant driver, boosting ASR to 87.43%, a 75.84%                     We proposed DGSIP, a multimodal jailbreak framework that
improvement over the baseline. This gain validates our                    combines gradient-free su!x search with image-phrase in-
hypothesis that predictive dissonance provides a powerful,                jection. DGSIP leverages predictive dissonance to identify

   When both modules are integrated, DGSIP achieves the                   guiding su!x optimization. It further strengthens the at-
highest 96.37% ASR. The additional improvement over the                   tack by using optimized image-embedded phrases to lever-
text-only variant underscores the complementary value of                  age cross-modal fusion. Our analysis reveals a key finding:
the image–phrase module. It helps the attack escape local                 reusing safety-suppressed tokens can reliably reactivate un-
optima where textual exploration stagnates and pushes the                 safe behaviors and transfer across di”erent VLMs, exposing
model toward more severe safety violations, highlighting the              hidden vulnerabilities in multimodal alignment. Evaluations
necessity of joint multimodal optimization.                               under white-box and black-box conditions show that DGSIP
